objective_strength.title: Clinician-led Social proof is current, treatment-specific and decision-useful.

binding_constraint.title: Local Search cannot reliably surface the treatment proof already present elsewhere.
binding_constraint.statement: Local Search cannot reliably surface the treatment proof already present on Social. Geo-grid visibility and incomplete GBP treatment categories keep high-intent patients from encountering the practice beyond its immediate address.

top_priorities.title: Correct the priority-treatment local discovery gap.
top_priorities.impact: High-intent local demand is least likely to encounter the fictional practice beyond its immediate address.
top_priorities.why_now: High-intent local demand is least likely to encounter the practice beyond its immediate address.
top_priorities.expected_effect: A measured geo-grid baseline would show where discovery fails so later profile work is aimed at the actual leak, not a ranking guarantee.

top_priorities.title: Align GBP treatments and categories with the priority offer.
top_priorities.impact: A clearer profile taxonomy would connect the existing proof to matching search intent.
top_priorities.why_now: The public profile still gives search platforms an incomplete view of the priority offer.
top_priorities.expected_effect: Accurate GBP categories and services can connect existing proof to matching search intent, without promising a visibility outcome.

top_priorities.title: Carry clinician proof into high-intent Search and Website decisions.
top_priorities.impact: The strongest evidence currently loses continuity before the booking decision.
top_priorities.why_now: The strongest clinician evidence currently loses continuity before the booking decision.
top_priorities.expected_effect: Carrying approved proof into high-intent pages would reduce the drop between attention and enquiry, without forecasting patient volume.

do_not_do.title: Do not increase paid traffic until local treatment discovery and proof continuity are corrected.
do_not_do.rationale: Paid ads and extra traffic would send more people into a market where the practice is not discoverable for priority treatments, amplifying the same search-visibility leak.
revisit_after: Priority-treatment geo-grid cells recover to a useful local result set
GBP categories and services match the approved treatment catalogue

remediation_tasks.outcome: Priority-treatment visibility is measured from a reproducible geo-grid and the weakest cells have an evidence-backed correction plan.
steps: Freeze the priority treatment, city query, grid centre, five-mile radius and named comparison set.
Export the 5×5 baseline and label the cells where the practice falls outside the useful local result set.
Check each weak cell against GBP category, treatment and entity evidence before documenting the corrective action.
Repeat the same grid after the accepted changes and compare like-for-like evidence.

sequence.rationale: The baseline defines where discovery fails and prevents unrelated search work from being treated as the first fix.

remediation_tasks.owner_role: Local search specialist, with an owner approving the priority treatment and market
remediation_tasks.effort_complexity: Medium — one controlled measurement set plus evidence review; coordination rises if entity records conflict.
remediation_tasks.implementation_risk: Changing the profile from one grid snapshot can damage relevance; preserve the query method and require corroborating profile evidence.
remediation_tasks.horizon: Baseline in days; observable local movement may require several weeks and is not guaranteed.
acceptance_evidence: Dated 5×5 export with query, centre, radius and competitors
remediation_tasks.next_action: Approve the one priority treatment and exact local query for the baseline.

remediation_tasks.outcome: The public GBP categories and services accurately represent the approved priority treatments without stuffing or unsupported claims.
steps: Export the current primary category, secondary categories and service inventory.
Compare that inventory with the approved treatment catalogue and the named local comparison set.
Draft the smallest accurate category and service changes, including owner review for naming and compliance.
Publish accepted changes and capture the live profile state.
prerequisites_access: GBP manager access for the chosen implementer

sequence.rationale: The geo-grid baseline fixes the comparison method before the GBP taxonomy changes are published.

remediation_tasks.owner_role: GBP/local search specialist with owner approval
remediation_tasks.effort_complexity: Medium — straightforward configuration when access and naming are clean; higher if duplicates or category conflicts emerge.
remediation_tasks.implementation_risk: Unsupported services, keyword stuffing or category churn can reduce trust; use only accurate public treatments and retain a before state.
remediation_tasks.horizon: Implementation within days; indexing and visibility response can take longer.
remediation_tasks.next_action: Export the current GBP category and service inventory.

remediation_tasks.outcome: The same verifiable clinician proof appears at the high-intent Search-to-Website decision points without adding unsupported claims.
steps: Inventory the strongest approved clinician proof already visible on Social.
Map each proof item to the relevant treatment page and public profile destination.
Add attribution, clinician context and a clear next step at the chosen decision points.
Test the mobile journey from discovery to the proof and booking action.
prerequisites_access: Approved proof assets and usage permission

sequence.rationale: Proof is carried into the corrected treatment taxonomy after the discovery path has a stable destination.

remediation_tasks.owner_role: Content strategist and web implementer, with clinician/compliance acceptance
remediation_tasks.effort_complexity: Medium to high — requires asset permissions, content adaptation, web changes and cross-surface QA.
remediation_tasks.implementation_risk: Proof can become misleading when context or permission is lost; retain attribution and obtain approval before publication.
remediation_tasks.horizon: One to three weeks depending on asset permission and website release cadence.
remediation_tasks.next_action: Select the two strongest attributable clinician-proof assets for the priority treatment.

roadmap_preview.disclaimer: Illustrative sequencing based on this diagnosis. Final Sprint scope is confirmed separately.

implementation_paths.diy: Assign the listed owner roles internally, follow task sequence 1–3 and retain every acceptance artifact in one shared evidence folder.
implementation_paths.other_provider: Give another local-search and web team this report, the metric evidence and task IDs; require them to return the same acceptance evidence without re-hiding the method.
implementation_paths.defer: Preserve the dated baseline, monitor the two lower-priority items and repeat the same collection method before making a later decision.
implementation_paths.caesthetic: Ask CAESTHETIC to scope only the selected tasks, access, owners and acceptance checks in a separate written Sprint agreement.

why_caesthetic.evidence_advantage: CAESTHETIC has already assembled the synthetic case method, evidence references and dependency order, so a real-case team would not need to restart diagnosis.
why_caesthetic.coordination_advantage: The work crosses local search, content, web implementation and compliance acceptance; one coordinator can reduce handoff cost while keeping specialist accountability visible.
why_caesthetic.sprint_boundary: The Growth Score is not purchased Sprint scope. A 30-Day Sprint includes only tasks, dependencies and acceptance evidence confirmed later in writing, with no ranking, enquiry or revenue guarantee.
why_caesthetic.ownership: The owner keeps the report, evidence pack and complete task plan and may implement it in-house, use another provider, defer it or stop. There is no lock-in.
